tool.name: ATRIUM born-digital converter
tool.description: turns a PDF, DOCX or XLSX into an ATRIUM document record and Markdown
tool.command:
#import re ## The record's doc_id comes from the file name: the document is linked under its collection name, ## with its format's extension (the converter reads the format from the bytes, not the name). #set $stem = re.sub(r'\.(pdf|docx|xlsx)$', '', str($document.element_identifier), flags=re.IGNORECASE) #set $stem = re.sub(r'[^\w.\-]', '_', $stem) or 'document' export TMPDIR="\${_GALAXY_JOB_TMP_DIR:-\$PWD/tmp}" && mkdir -p input "\$TMPDIR" && ln -s '$document' 'input/${stem}.${document.ext}' &&
python3 /app/api_util/digital_to_json.py 'input/${stem}.${document.ext}' --document-json-out record.json #if $baseline: --document-json '$baseline' #end if --docx-page-breaks '$docx_page_breaks' #if $write_markdown: --markdown record.md #end if --paradata-dir paradata && mv record.json '$record' && #if $write_markdown: mv record.md '$markdown' && #end if mv paradata/*_digital-convert.json '$paradata'

param.name: document
param.label: Born-digital document
param.help: A PDF with a text layer, a Word document (DOCX) or a spreadsheet (XLSX). For a collection, the tool runs once per document.

param.name: docx_page_breaks
param.label: Pages of a DOCX
param.help: A DOCX has no fixed pages; this decides where a page ends. Ignored for PDF and XLSX.
param.option: Explicit breaks, and Word's own rendered breaks where it saved them
The whole document as one page

param.name: write_markdown
param.label: Also write Markdown
param.help: The record rendered as Markdown, one section per page, with layout cues as HTML comments.

param.name: baseline
param.label: Document record to add to
param.help: An ATRIUM document record from an earlier stage; its doc_id is kept.

has_text.text: Excavation report, block one, line one.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Reads a born-digital document, a file that was written on a computer rather than scanned, and writes its text, pages, lines and tables as an ATRIUM document record. It runs the ATRIUM born-digital converter (`ufal/atrium-digital-convert`_), release @TOOL_VERSION@, with its light engine: no models and no network.
**Input**
- *PDF* with a text layer. Each page is checked: a page with no text, or with text that does not decode, is flagged ``needs_ocr`` in the record, so that it can be sent to OCR. - *DOCX*: headings, paragraphs and tables. The pages follow the *Pages of a DOCX* setting. - *XLSX*: one page per sheet, one line per row.
A PDF that already carries an OCR run's invisible text over page images is refused (exit 3): send it to OCR post-processing instead. A broken or encrypted file stops with exit 4.
**Outputs**
- *Document record* (JSON): the ATRIUM document record, with ``source``, ``pages`` (each with its ``text_layer`` and a ``quality_band``), ``content``, ``lines`` and ``tables``. - *Markdown*: the record as Markdown, one ``## Page N`` section per page, with ``<!-- BBOX -->`` layout cues for PDF lines. - *Paradata* (JSON): the run's provenance, with the components and their licences.
**Licence**
The code is MIT; the paradata lists each component's licence.
.. _`ufal/atrium-digital-convert`: https://github.com/ufal/atrium-digital-convert
